title: Capture the real import graph during profiling, so a change to an import-only module selects its importers instead of the whole suite
description:
so-d8v gave the profile per-test files_covered and top-level measured_files. That fixes the REASONING for a changed file no test executes at runtime, but not the SELECTION: a Pydantic model or constants module that only ever runs at import time still forces a full-suite run, because coverage records import-time execution under the empty context and never records WHO imported it.

The missing relation is the import graph. With it, a changed import-only module selects the tests whose modules transitively import it, which measurement shows is a 60-83% saving over running everything (see NOTES).

Scope of this issue is CAPTURE ONLY -- record the graph into the profile. Consuming it for selection is so-jr5.
acceptance_criteria: A profile recorded from a suite where module A imports module B, and module C also imports B with A collected first, contains BOTH the A->B and C->B edges. A module imported only at collection time (never executed under any test context) still has its importers recorded. Edges resolve to project-relative file paths; site-packages and .venv are excluded.
notes:
MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES THIS (2026-09-06). Percentage of the suite an import
closure selects, computed per source file, via a --collect-only prototype:

repo                tests  files   p25    median   p75    max     mean
smoke-optimiser        81     19  18.5%   27.2%   48.1%  87.7%   33.3%
casey_ai/api         1389    143  20.5%   47.7%   52.1%  96.5%   39.4%
enphase_curtailer    2600    271   7.3%   12.8%   21.9%  93.2%   17.5%

Against the current 100% fallback that is a 60-83% saving on exactly the edits
that trigger a full run today.

The decisive case is casey_ai: db/models/common.py reaches 96.5% of the suite
(genuinely global, running everything IS right), while db/models/interval.py and
db/models/task.py reach 3 tests each (0.2%) -- same directory, same kind of
declaration file, not re-exported through the package __init__. Today all three
are treated identically. The graph gets both right.

CAVEAT ON THE NUMBERS: measured with --collect-only, which misses imports made
lazily inside test function bodies, so real closures may be marginally wider.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DECISIONS 2026-09-06 (user, answering the open questions in DESIGN):

1. ERROR POLICY: swallow-and-count. Edge recording catches, increments a counter
and keeps the first N exception reprs; both land in the profile so a degraded
graph is visible to so-jr5 rather than silently under-selecting. Costs one
documented noqa BLE001, matching the precedent in smoke_optimiser/plugin.py.

2. CODE LOCATION: a real typed module, smoke_optimiser/profiler/import_tracer.py,
imported normally. NOT the PYTEST_HOOK_CODE inline string. Decisive fact:
pyproject.toml already registers smoke_optimiser.plugin as a pytest11 entry
point, and the runner invokes sys.executable -m pytest, so smoke_optimiser is
ALREADY imported into every profiled run -- the dependency-free-subprocess
argument for the inline string is void. The win is unit-testability of the
edge-resolution arithmetic (level>1 relative imports becomes a 3-line test
rather than a nested fixture project run end to end), which matters because the
bug class here is a MISSING edge: it raises nothing and is invisible to an e2e
test.

3. MECHANISMS: implement BOTH the builtins.__import__ wrapper and the
sys.meta_path finder for importlib.import_module first-loads, in this issue.

4. XDIST: fix so-u3i FIRST, then implement edge capture consistently with the
write/merge path it establishes. so-u3i is now decided: support xdist, per-worker
files merged by the runner, runtime detection (not arg sniffing), worker count
recorded in the profile, and the TIME-based optimiser errors on a parallel
profile while map-only consumers stay silent.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS 2026-09-06 (user), on top of the four already recorded:

5. THREE MECHANISMS, not two:
   - builtins.__import__ wrapper: every execution of an import statement, importer
     from globals["__name__"]. Primary.
   - importlib.import_module wrapper: import_module bypasses builtins.__import__
     entirely. Importer comes from the CALLER FRAME (sys._getframe), which is
     unambiguous at the call site, and it fires on every call rather than only on
     first load. Chosen over stack-walking inside find_spec, which would have to
     skip a variable number of importlib bootstrap frames and misattributes when
     the import happens inside a helper in another module.
   - sys.meta_path finder: the wider net for first loads through entry points
     neither wrapper sees (importlib.util, pkgutil, C-level __import__).

6. THE FINDER RECORDS LOADS, NOT EDGES. find_spec receives no globals, so it
   cannot know the importer, and NO frame heuristic is used to guess one. It
   records the module name only. At snapshot time any PROJECT module that was
   loaded but has zero importer edges is reported as unattributed_modules.
   so-jr5 must treat a change to one of those files as "cannot answer" -> run the
   full suite, NOT as "nothing imports it" -> select nothing. A wrong edge
   over-selects quietly; a missing edge under-selects silently, which is the exact
   failure this issue exists to prevent, so the blind spot is made loud instead of
   guessed at.

7. INSTALLED FROM THE PROFILING HOOK (_smoke_hook, passed with -p by the runner),
   not from the shipped smoke_optimiser/plugin.py. plugin.py is loaded by the
   pytest11 entry point into EVERY pytest run of every project that installs
   smoke-optimiser, so installing there would need an env-var gate to stay inert;
   the profiling-only plugin needs no gate and keeps profiling concerns out of the
   --smoke filter. Both are loaded at pytest startup, so both are early enough to
   precede collection.

8. XDIST: follows the path so-u3i established -- one graph file per worker,
   suffixed by PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER, unioned by the runner. Edges are a set, so the
   merge is a plain union; error and load counts sum.
close_reason: Import graph captured into the profile. Three-part graph (edges, unattributed_modules, resolution_errors) built from wrapping builtins.__import__ and importlib.import_module. Verified serial and under 3 xdist workers: identical 91-edge graph, all acceptance criteria covered by tests.

title: Files with no branches never appear in the coverage map, so change-based selection cannot see them
description:
ProfilingOutcome.branches_covered holds branch ids only. so-jr5 plans to invert
that map to get file -> tests, but a source file containing NO BRANCHES produces
no branch ids at all, so it is absent from the map entirely.

Straight-line code is common and exactly the kind that has no branches:
constants modules, __init__.py re-export files, dataclass and Pydantic model
definitions, thin delegating wrappers, protocol/ABC declarations. In this
repository smoke_optimiser/profiler/models.py and optimiser/models.py are both
pure declaration files.

CONSEQUENCE FOR so-jr5. Its fallback rule is 'a file with no entry in the map
means new code, so run everything'. A branchless file hits that rule and
triggers a full-suite run despite being neither new nor untested. The result is
SAFE but WRONG in its reasoning, and it fires on ordinary edits to model files,
which undermines the value of change-based selection precisely where it should
be cheapest. Worse, the fallback message will tell the user the file is new when
it is not.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: total_branches is derived from coverage's per-file analysis,
so a branchless file contributes nothing to the denominator either. Nothing is
miscounted -- the file is simply invisible.

OPTIONS.
1. Record a separate per-test file set alongside branches_covered, populated
   from the arc table's file_id for every executed arc regardless of whether it
   is a branch. Cheap: the ingest already streams every arc row, and the profile
   grows by roughly one path per test-file pair.
2. Distinguish 'file has no branches' from 'file not in the map' so so-jr5 can
   answer for branchless files without the full-suite fallback.

Option 1 also removes so-jr5's dependence on branch data for its file mapping,
which is a better fit for a feature whose granularity is deliberately
file-level.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::read_coverage_db (the per-arc
loop already has file_id in hand); smoke_optimiser/profiler/models.py for the
profile format.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that imports and calls into a branchless module can be found
by asking the map which tests touched that module's file.
close_reason: Added per-test files_covered and top-level measured_files to the profile

title: Coverage recorded during fixture setup aborts the entire profiling run
description:
REGRESSION introduced by so-mr0. A single test whose fixture executes measured source and then errors kills the whole profiling run.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-06 on a 2-test throwaway project:

  @pytest.fixture
  def broken():
      classify(-1)                 # exercises measured source during setup
      raise RuntimeError('boom')

  def test_setup_error(broken): ...

  $ smoke-optimiser --src app
  1 passed, 1 error in 0.02s
  ❌ Error: 1 coverage context matches no test that pytest collected in this run:
    test_edge.py::test_setup_error

WHY. coverage records a context per test PHASE, so the fixture's coverage lands
under 'test_edge.py::test_setup_error|setup'. But PYTEST_HOOK_CODE in
runner.py only records a report when report.when == 'call':

    if report.when == 'call':
        item.config._smoke_outcomes[item.nodeid] = {...}

A test that errors during setup never reaches its call phase, so it is absent
from test_durations. coverage_db._verify_contexts then finds a context matching
no collected test and raises, by design -- that fail-loudly check is correct and
should stay. The bug is that the test IS real and WAS collected; the hook simply
did not record it.

TWO THINGS ARE WRONG.
1. One errored fixture takes down a whole profiling run of any size.
2. The error message misdiagnoses it, telling the user the coverage database is
   stale and to 'remove it and profile again', which will fail identically.

NOT A PROBLEM: skipped tests, and setup errors in fixtures that touch no
measured source, both produce no context row at all (verified), so they do not
trigger this.

LIKELY FIX. Record setup/teardown phase reports in the hook so such tests appear
with passed=False. Failing tests are already hard-excluded by the optimiser
(PRD 5.5), so an errored test would be excluded by the existing path rather than
being a fatal ingest error. Needs a decision on duration (setup time only? zero?)
and on whether a teardown failure after a passing call should flip passed.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py PYTEST_HOOK_CODE; the check is
smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::_verify_contexts.

ACCEPTANCE: a suite containing a fixture that errors after touching measured
source profiles successfully, and tests/test_e2e.py covers it -- the current e2e
project has only cleanly-passing tests and would not catch this.
close_reason: Fixed by recording failed setup/teardown-phase reports in the pytest hook, so setup-erroring tests get an outcome entry instead of leaving an orphaned coverage context. Added regression coverage in tests/test_e2e.py.

title: Add change-based test selection: run every test that has ever executed a line in a changed file
description:
smoke-optimiser today selects a STATIC subset: highest coverage per second,
the same tests whatever you changed. That is a coverage bet -- it cannot
promise the coverage it skips, so it cannot gate a commit.

This adds a second, honest selection mode. Given a diff, run every test that
has ever executed a line in a changed file. The promise is literally statable,
which is the whole point: "every test that has ever executed a line you touched".

WHY IT IS POSSIBLE. The profiling data already IS a test-impact map -- the
missing piece that made file-globbing and pytest markers the only options
before. ProfilingOutcome.branches_covered holds branch ids formatted as
'{file}:{u}->{v}' (parser.py:127), so inverting the map gives file -> tests.

MEASURED on enphase_curtailer, 2026-09-06: 2600 tests, 190 files in the map,
MEDIAN 37 TESTS PER FILE. Touch one source file and you run ~37 of 2600 tests.
The full suite is 55s warm on a 10-core Mac and 7m32s on GitHub CI's 4 cores.

GRANULARITY: FILE-LEVEL. Deliberately not line-level. Line numbers shift the
moment you insert a line above, so a line-level map silently mismatches after
almost any edit. File-level is immune to line shifts, reformatting and
refactors within a file. Line-level with git-aware remapping is a later option
-- ship the robust one and measure what it actually saves first.

FALLBACK: FULL SUITE, PLUS A STALENESS EXPIRY. Any input the map cannot answer
for means run everything, and say why. At minimum:
  - a file with no entry in the map (new code -- exactly when tests matter most)
  - a changed test file or conftest.py
  - a dependency or lockfile change
  - a profile older than the expiry
The expiry exists because auto-regeneration triggers on a MISSING map, not a
stale one: a map that is present but no longer matches the code would silently
under-select forever. Never let it degrade to best-effort -- the moment it
selects a subset it cannot justify, it is test-fast again and cannot gate.

REGENERATION MUST NEVER BLOCK A COMMIT. The map is gitignored, not committed.
Absent or expired means "run the full suite now, regenerate in the background",
so the developer never pays more than the full suite they would have run anyway
and the map is simply fresh next time. Profiling instrumentation is cheap --
measured +11% on enphase (61s -> 68s with --cov-context=test) -- but a
regeneration is still a full suite run, and having that fire mid-commit at an
unpredictable moment is worse than a steady wait.

DOES NOT COVER, and must not pretend to: npm/vitest suites, tsc typechecks,
codegen drift checks, Rust. In casey_ai the heavy precommit item is a Docker
integration suite; only the Python half is in scope here.

Blocked on so-mr0: the map cannot be built for a suite this size until the
ingest stops loading a 1.2 GB JSON file into memory.
notes:
INPUT FROM so-aeo (2026-09-07): the profile now carries import_graph, with three parts.

* edges: (importer, imported) as project-relative file paths. Invert and take the
  transitive closure to get every test module that depends on a changed file.
* unattributed_modules: project files loaded during the run that NOTHING was seen
  to import -- test modules, conftest.py, and any pytest11 plugin belonging to the
  project (pytest loads entry-point plugins before any hook can watch). A change to
  one of these means the graph CANNOT ANSWER. It must fall back to the full suite.
  Reading it as 'nothing imports this' selects zero tests, which is the silent
  under-selection this whole line of work exists to prevent.
* resolution_errors / error_samples: edge recording that failed and was swallowed,
  because raising inside __import__ would kill the user's test run. Non-zero means
  the graph is incomplete by an unknown amount -- decide whether selection should
  refuse to trust it, the way the time-based half refuses a parallel profile.

Measured on smoke-optimiser itself: 91 edges, 17 unattributed of ~35 project files.

title: Replace the 1.2 GB JSON coverage ingest with a direct read of coverage.py's SQLite database
description:
smoke-optimiser cannot profile a medium suite today. Measured against
enphase_curtailer (2600 tests, 230 files) on 2026-09-06:

  coverage json --show-contexts    1.2 GB
  the same data as .coverage       29 MB      (40x smaller)
  the same report WITHOUT contexts 1.9 MB in 1.3s

parser.py:193 does a single json.load() of that 1.2 GB file, which needs many
GB of resident Python objects. The contexts are 99.8% of the file.

WHAT TO BUILD. Read coverage.py's SQLite database directly instead. One query
joining arc -> context -> file extracted the full test->arc map in 0.43s and
yielded exactly 2600 tests, matching the collected count:

  select context.context, file.path, arc.fromno, arc.tono
    from arc join context on arc.context_id = context.id
             join file    on arc.file_id    = file.id
   where context.context != ''

The public CoverageData API is NOT viable: set_query_contexts()/arcs() over 40
contexts took 6.51s, extrapolating to 13.4 minutes for this suite. Raw SQL is
~1900x faster. That is why this reads an internal schema.

TWO CORRECTNESS BUGS THIS FIXES.

1. parser.py:139 infers branch coverage: a test covers u->v if it executed line
   u and line v. That over-attributes -- both endpoints can execute without that
   arc ever being taken. The arc table holds real arcs, so the inference and its
   docstring caveat both go away.
2. TestResolver (parser.py:37-77) matches coverage contexts to node ids by
   endswith/startswith and by bare function name. Contexts are already exact node
   ids with a phase suffix ('tests/test_x.py::test_y|run'), so rsplit('|', 1)[0]
   is exact. The fuzzy matcher can mis-attribute coverage between same-named
   tests in different files; delete it.

SCHEMA COUPLING. The DB format is not a public API. Read the coverage_schema
table (version 7 as of coverage 7.13) and compare against a verified set. On a
mismatch, FAIL LOUDLY -- silently mis-reading would silently under-select tests,
which is the worst failure this tool can have. The error must name the schema
version found, the versions supported, the installed coverage.py version, and
say plainly that smoke-optimiser itself needs updating to support the new schema,
with the file to edit. Do not degrade quietly.

THE DENOMINATOR. The arc table records only arcs that were EXECUTED, so a
never-taken branch has no row. enphase has 3198 branches, 406 uncovered; counting
from SQLite alone reports 100% instead of 88%. --target-cov needs the true total,
so keep a SECOND context-free `coverage json` purely for totals -- 1.9 MB and 1.3s,
because the blow-up was entirely contexts. total_branches keeps its current
meaning (executed + missing).

Everything moves to the SQLite ingest, not just the new selection feature, so the
tool has one ingest path rather than two. Retire parse_coverage_json, TestResolver,
the CoverageReport/CoverageFile models, the [json] show_contexts rcfile setting,
and the contexts export step in runner.py:159-176.

Also handle a suite profiled WITHOUT branch mode: that data lands in line_bits
(a bitmap blob), not arc. Either support it or refuse with a clear message.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED with two departures from the original description, both agreed with the user.

1. NO SECOND coverage json. The description called for a context-free 'coverage json'
purely for the denominator. Not needed: the denominator is computed in-process from
coverage's own per-file analysis (FileReporter.arcs() filtered to branch lines), in the
same pass that builds the arc translation map. Measured 0.03s on this repo. Verified
byte-identical to 'coverage json' on both sets (denominator 234/234, executed 153/153),
and the 222-branch total matches pytest-cov's own report exactly. One ingest, no
subprocess, no JSON, no absolute-vs-relative path reconciliation between two sources.

2. RAW ARCS NEED TRANSLATING -- not mentioned in the original description, and the
landmine in it. The arc table records the interpreter's actual jump targets; coverage
reports branches in an AST-derived vocabulary. A jump into the middle of a multi-line
statement is reported against the statement's first line, so raw 3->6 is reported as
3->5. Intersecting raw arcs against reported branches without translation silently
dropped ~4% of this repo's executed branches -- exactly the silent under-selection the
issue exists to prevent. Fixed by running each file's distinct raw arcs through
FileReporter.translate_arcs ONCE, building a raw->branch lookup, then a dict hit per
arc. This is what sidesteps the 13.4-minute per-context path.

3. UNATTRIBUTABLE BRANCHES. Module-level code runs at import under the empty context,
so no test can ever claim it (4 branches on this repo). The old inference-based parser
falsely attributed these to whichever test touched the lines. They are now kept in
total_branches (so it keeps agreeing with 'coverage report') and surfaced as a new
ProfilingData.unattributable_branches field, with the summary reporting the attainable
ceiling: 'Ceiling: 98.2% max attainable'.

FAIL-LOUDLY paths, all tested: unsupported coverage_schema version (names version found,
supported set, installed coverage.py, and the file to edit), line-only data (has_arcs=0),
a context matching no collected test, a source file no longer readable, a corrupt or
non-coverage database, an empty coverage_schema table.

FOR so-jr5: branch ids are relative to project_root (POSIX), so they match git diff paths
directly. Note the file->test map only covers files that contain branches.
close_reason: Implemented: SQLite ingest with arc translation, in-process denominator, fail-loudly schema and context checks. Verified byte-identical to coverage json; 76 tests pass; ruff/ty clean.

title: The .smoke_suite.json schema describes a coverage-per-second suite, not a change-based selection
description:
The pytest plugin's --smoke mode reads .smoke_suite.json and filters collection to the node ids in it (smoke_optimiser/plugin.py). That is the natural execution path for change-based selection too -- but the file's schema is entirely about the OTHER half of the tool.

SmokeSuiteFile (smoke_optimiser/reports/smoke_suite.py) requires a SummaryModel
with total_branches, full_suite_branches_covered, smoke_branches_covered,
smoke_coverage_pct, full_suite_runtime_s and smoke_suite_runtime_s, a
SmokeConfigModel with time_cap and target_cov, and per-test SelectedTestModel
entries carrying duration_s, branches_covered, marginal_branches and efficiency.

None of that exists for a change-based selection. There is no time cap, no
coverage target, and no efficiency ranking -- the promise is categorical ('every
test that has ever executed a line you touched'), not a coverage bet. Filling
those fields with zeros would make the plugin's report header announce '0.0%
coverage' for a selection that is not making a coverage claim at all.

The decision is whether change-based selection:
  * writes the same file with a mode discriminator and optional summary blocks,
    keeping one plugin path and one --smoke flag;
  * writes its own file with its own schema and its own flag; or
  * bypasses the file entirely and prints node ids for the caller to pass to pytest.

Bears on the plugin's report header and its 'smoke test not found in collection'
warning too, both of which currently assume the coverage-suite framing. Worth
settling before so-jr5 is implemented rather than after.

title: Define what 'changed files' means for change-based selection: staged vs worktree, renames, deletions
description:
so-jr5 says 'given a diff' and never says which one. The obvious first use is a precommit hook running over STAGED files, and that choice has consequences the design does not yet cover.

WHICH DIFF. git diff --cached --name-only is the staged set; git diff --name-only
is the unstaged set; git diff <ref>...HEAD is a branch's worth. A precommit hook
must use --cached, or it selects tests for edits the developer deliberately left
out of the commit while ignoring ones they staged. Whether unstaged changes should
also be included (they affect what the tests will actually execute, since pytest
reads the worktree, not the index) is a real question with a defensible answer
either way -- and a wrong one silently tests something other than what is being
committed.

RENAMES. With -M, git reports a rename as a single R entry old -> new. The
profile's maps only know the OLD path. Treating the new path as an unknown file
means the full-suite fallback, which is safe but wasteful for what is often a
pure move; treating it as the old path reuses the map correctly. Without -M the
same change appears as an add plus a delete, which lands in yet another branch of
the logic.

DELETIONS. A deleted file has map entries but no longer exists. The tests that
executed it are exactly the ones most likely to break, so they must still be
selected -- the naive 'does this path exist' check would drop them.

NON-SOURCE FILES. so-jr5 already lists dependency and lockfile changes as
full-suite triggers. The broader rule needs stating: any staged path the map
cannot reason about (YAML, templates, static assets, .github workflows) means
'cannot answer', not 'affects nothing'.

This is a decision issue, not an implementation one -- it should be settled before
so-jr5 is built, since each answer changes the shape of the input handling.

title: Changed-file paths from git are repo-relative, but the profile's paths are cwd-relative
description:
Change-based selection (so-jr5) has to match a list of changed files against the profile's maps. The two sides do not agree on what a path is relative to.

* git reports paths relative to the REPOSITORY ROOT (git rev-parse --show-toplevel),
  whatever directory the command was run from.
* The profile stores paths relative to PROJECT_ROOT, which cli.py sets to
  Path.cwd() (smoke_optimiser/cli.py, 'project_root = Path.cwd()'). coverage_db
  makes measured_files and files_covered relative to it, and the import tracer is
  handed the same root via SMOKE_PROJECT_ROOT.

These coincide only when smoke-optimiser is run from the repository root. They
differ whenever it is run from a subdirectory, and permanently in a monorepo where
the Python project is one directory of a larger repo -- exactly the layout where
selecting a subset matters most.

FAILURE MODE. Nothing errors. A staged path like 'services/api/db/models.py' is
simply absent from a map keyed by 'db/models.py', so it matches nothing, and the
selection returns no tests for a file that plenty of tests depend on. Silent
under-selection, which is the failure this tool must never have.

Note that the fallback does not save us either: 'a file with no entry in the map'
is supposed to mean 'new code -> run everything', so a systematic path mismatch
would look like every changed file being new, which at least fails safe -- but
only until something optimises that fallback away. The mismatch should be
resolved, not relied upon.

WHERE. smoke_optimiser/cli.py (project_root), smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py
(relative_to), smoke_optimiser/profiler/import_tracer.py (snapshot's relative_to),
and whatever reads the git diff in so-jr5.

NEEDS A DECISION on which root wins, and on whether a profile should record the
root its paths are relative to so a mismatch can be detected rather than assumed
away.

title: A missing import graph file is indistinguishable from a graph with no edges
description:
_read_iteration_graph (smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py) globs the temp directory for graph files, reads what it finds, and merges them:

    paths = sorted(import_graph_json.parent.glob(...))
    graphs = [read_graph(path) for path in paths]
    return merge_graphs(graphs)

With NO files present that is merge_graphs([]), which returns a perfectly valid
ImportGraph with no edges, no unattributed modules and no errors. Nothing raises.

WHY THAT IS DANGEROUS. An empty graph does not read as 'unknown', it reads as
'nothing in this project imports anything'. Every file then looks like a file no
module depends on, so change-based selection (so-jr5) would select no tests for a
change to any of them -- the silent under-selection this whole line of work
exists to prevent. Contrast the sibling path: _read_iteration_outcomes raises
OutcomesIngestError on an unreadable file, and a malformed graph raises
ImportGraphIngestError. Only ABSENCE is silent.

WHEN IT HAPPENS. pytest_unconfigure writes the graph, and it does not run if the
process is hard-killed (timeout, OOM, SIGKILL) -- see so-fp4 for the same class
of problem in the coverage database. Under xdist it is worse and more likely: one
killed worker means one missing file, so the merged graph silently lacks that
worker's edges while looking complete.

NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION. The runner knows how many graph files it should expect
in the serial case (exactly one), but under xdist it only learns the worker count
from the outcomes files it reads in the same iteration. Options: require at least
one graph file per iteration and error otherwise; cross-check the graph file count
against the worker count the outcomes reported; or have the hook write a sentinel
early so absence is detectable. Whatever is chosen, absence must not be silent.

title: CLI boolean defaults silently clobber the same setting from pyproject.toml
description:
resolve_config (smoke_optimiser/config.py) applies a CLI override whenever the value 'is not None'. Typer boolean flags default to False, not None, so they are ALWAYS applied.

Concretely: a project with

  [tool.smoke_optimiser]
  allow_ordered = true

still gets allow_ordered=False on every run that does not pass --allow-ordered, because the CLI's default False overrides it. The setting is silently inert -- the user sees the pytest-randomly error they configured away.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/cli.py builds cli_overrides with 'allow_ordered': allow_ordered; smoke_optimiser/config.py resolve_config's 'value is not None' loop.

The new --allow-parallel-durations flag (so-u3i) deliberately avoids this by passing 'allow_parallel_durations or None', which is the shape every boolean flag should use -- or resolve_config should learn which keys are booleans whose False means 'unset'. Pick one and apply it consistently.

NOT a theory: verified by reading the resolution loop, and the reason the new flag was written differently from its neighbour.

title: Fix lint errors after switching ruff to select=ALL
description: pyproject now selects ALL ruff rules; 55 errors across source, scripts and tests need fixing without editing lint rules.

title: Change-based selection must treat a changed conftest.py as affecting every test at or below its directory
description:
conftest.py is never imported by test modules -- pytest loads it itself -- so it has no edge in the import graph so-aeo captures, and its fixtures leave no distinguishing mark in files_covered either. Change-based selection would therefore see a changed conftest.py as affecting nothing, which UNDER-selects: silently skipping tests whose fixtures just changed is the worst failure this tool can have.

pytest's own rule is directory scope: a conftest.py applies to every test collected at or below the directory containing it. Mirror exactly that rule.
design:
Pure path-prefix matching against the collected test node ids, which already begin with a project-relative file path. For a changed file whose name is exactly 'conftest.py', select every test whose node id path is equal to or below that conftest's directory. A repository-root conftest.py therefore selects the whole suite, which is correct.

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE -- these are separate, harder problems and must NOT be attempted here:
  - pytest_plugins declarations, which can load a conftest from an unrelated directory and break the directory-scope assumption.
  - Plugins supplied via -p on the command line.
  - Fixture-level granularity (working out WHICH fixtures a test actually used).
If the implementation starts needing any of these, stop and re-scope the issue rather than guessing.

Do not attempt to resolve a conftest's own imports here either; a conftest that imports a changed helper module is covered by so-aeo's graph, since conftest.py is itself an importer.
acceptance_criteria: A changed tests/sub/conftest.py selects every test under tests/sub/ and no test outside it. A changed conftest.py at the project root selects the entire suite. A changed conftest.py selects those tests even though no test module imports it and it contributes nothing to files_covered.

title: Hard-killed tests (timeout/crash) still produce orphaned coverage contexts and a misleading 'stale database' error
description:
Related to so-pc5 but NOT fixed by it. so-pc5's fix records an outcome whenever pytest's own makereport hook fires for a failed setup/teardown phase. But if a test's process is killed outright mid-phase -- e.g. pytest-timeout sending SIGKILL/SIGTERM, an OOM kill, or a segfaulting C extension under test -- makereport never runs for that phase at all. coverage.py may still have flushed a context row for whatever ran before the kill, but PYTEST_HOOK_CODE.pytest_runtest_makereport gets no chance to record anything for that nodeid.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py PYTEST_HOOK_CODE; smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::_verify_contexts.

EFFECT: _verify_contexts still raises CoverageIngestError for that test id, and the message is still wrong for this cause specifically -- 'This usually means the coverage database is stale, or was combined across different runs; remove it and profile again' does not describe a hard-killed test, and removing the DB and re-profiling will reproduce the same failure if the kill is deterministic (e.g. a real timeout).

NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION: is this in scope to fix at all (vs. documenting it as a known limitation), and if so, how would we detect 'test process was killed' from the coverage DB side (no report was ever received) versus a genuinely stale/combined DB? At minimum the error message should stop asserting a single specific cause it cannot verify.

title: Multi-iteration duration averaging blends setup-phase duration from a differently-outcomed iteration
description:
Introduced by the so-pc5 fix (runner.py PYTEST_HOOK_CODE now also records failed setup/teardown reports).

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py, the iterations loop around lines 169-178:
  for nodeid, data in raw_outcomes.items():
      all_durations[nodeid].append(data['duration'])
      final_outcomes[nodeid] = data['passed']   # last iteration wins
      final_markers[nodeid] = frozenset(data['markers'])
avg_durations is then sum(all_durations[nodeid]) / len(...) across ALL iterations, unconditionally.

PROBLEM. With config.iterations > 1 and a flaky test whose fixture sometimes errors in setup:
  iteration 1: fixture errors in setup after doing 2.0s of work -> recorded passed=False, duration=2.0 (the setup phase duration)
  iteration 2: fixture succeeds, call passes in 0.01s -> recorded passed=True, duration=0.01
final_outcomes lands on passed=True (last iteration), but avg_durations averages 2.0 and 0.01 together (~1.0s) -- a passing test now reports a duration wildly inflated by an unrelated failing iteration's setup-phase timing.

Before so-pc5, failed iterations were absent from raw_outcomes entirely (the hook only recorded 'call'), so this contamination could not happen -- durations from failing iterations simply were not collected. so-pc5 fixed a real crash but reopened this averaging correctness gap as a side effect.

NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION: should durations only be averaged across iterations whose outcome matches final_outcomes (i.e. only average the 'passed' iterations' durations when the test ultimately counts as passed)? Or bucket durations by outcome and report the one matching final_outcomes? Or something else? This wasn't decided as part of so-pc5 since it's a distinct pre-existing averaging mechanism the fix newly interacts with.

title: Profiling ignores the project's own coverage config, inflating total_branches
description:
runner.py writes its own minimal rcfile and passes it as --cov-config, which
REPLACES the project's coverage configuration rather than extending it:

    COVERAGERC_CONTENT = '''
    [run]
    branch = True
    '''

So the project's own settings are silently discarded during profiling. Most
consequential is [report] exclude_lines. This repository's own pyproject.toml
has:

    exclude_lines = ['pragma: no cover', 'if TYPE_CHECKING:',
                     'def __repr__', 'raise NotImplementedError']

None of these apply while profiling. Branches the project has explicitly
declared un-coverable are therefore counted in total_branches, inflating the
denominator and depressing every reported coverage percentage. [run] omit and
[run] source are dropped for the same reason.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT A so-mr0 REGRESSION -- the old JSON path passed the same
rcfile to 'coverage json', so behaviour is unchanged. It is more VISIBLE now:
so-mr0 computes the denominator in-process from FileReporter using this rcfile,
so the exclusions are absent from both numerator and denominator, and
coverage_db is where the effect now lands.

INTERACTION WITH --target-cov: an inflated denominator makes a given
--target-cov harder to reach than the user intends, and can make a threshold
they set from 'coverage report' output unreachable.

DESIGN DECISION. Merging user config is not free: an omit or source setting that
conflicts with --src, or a dynamic_context already set to something other than
'test', would break profiling. Options are to layer our [run] settings over the
discovered config, or to read only [report] exclusions, or to keep replacing but
warn when the project has settings we are discarding.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py COVERAGERC_CONTENT; consumed by
smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::read_coverage_db via config_file.

ACCEPTANCE: a branch marked 'pragma: no cover' does not appear in
total_branches, and profiling still works for a project with no coverage
configuration at all.

title: pytest's exit code is ignored, so a collection error silently yields a partial smoke suite
description:
runner.py runs the suite with check=False and never inspects the return code:

    subprocess.run(pytest_cmd, cwd=project_root, check=False, env=env)

Exit code 1 (tests failed) is expected and correctly handled -- failing tests are
hard-excluded. But every other non-zero code is swallowed:

  2  interrupted (e.g. Ctrl-C, or --maxfail reached)
  3  internal error
  4  usage error (e.g. a bad --pytest-args value)
  5  no tests collected

A COLLECTION ERROR IN ONE FILE is the dangerous case. pytest still runs and
still writes coverage for everything it did collect, so profiling proceeds
happily and emits a smoke suite that is simply missing every test in the broken
file. The user gets a green-looking result that under-selects, with no
indication anything was skipped. That is precisely the silent under-selection
so-mr0 was written to eliminate -- so-mr0 closed the ingest hole but this one is
upstream of it and still open.

Exit 5 (no tests collected) is currently caught downstream by chance: no
coverage database means CoverageIngestError. The message will talk about a
missing database rather than about no tests being collected.

DECISION NEEDED on --iterations > 1: if iteration 3 of 5 is interrupted, is the
accumulated coverage still usable, or is the whole run void? Coverage
accumulates across iterations into one database, so a partial iteration
contributes real data but skews nothing except durations.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py:157

ACCEPTANCE: a project with one uncollectable test file fails loudly rather than
producing a smoke suite; exit code 1 still proceeds as it does today.

title: Measure the import tracer's overhead on a large suite
description:
so-aeo added an ImportTracer that replaces builtins.__import__ and importlib.import_module for the whole profiling run. Every execution of every import statement in the suite now goes through a Python-level wrapper that resolves the target name, walks its ancestors and updates a set.

The cost is UNMEASURED. On smoke-optimiser itself the suite is far too small and
too fast for the difference to be distinguishable from noise, so nothing here
tells us what it does to a real suite.

This matters because so-jr5's whole argument for regenerating the profile in the
background rests on profiling being cheap: it quotes a measured +11% for coverage
instrumentation on enphase_curtailer (61s -> 68s with --cov-context=test). If the
tracer adds materially to that, the trade-off changes, and the capture may need to
become optional rather than always-on.

WHAT TO DO. Profile a large suite (enphase_curtailer, 2600 tests, or casey_ai/api,
1389 tests) three ways -- plain, with coverage instrumentation only, and with
instrumentation plus the tracer -- and record the deltas. The comparison needs the
tracer to be switchable to run at all, which is itself a useful outcome: today it
installs unconditionally from the profiling hook.

If the overhead is small, record the number next to the +11% in so-jr5 and close
this. If it is not, file the follow-up to make capture optional.

title: The canonical repro command emitted --no-allow-ordered, which the CLI rejects
description:
build_repro_command emitted '--no-allow-ordered' when allow_ordered was off, but --allow-ordered is declared as a bare flag with no negative form. Pasting the 'Repro:' line printed in the summary therefore failed with 'No such option: --no-allow-ordered' -- the one command whose entire job is to reproduce the run did not run.

Verified before the fix:
  $ uv run smoke-optimiser --no-allow-ordered --optimise-only
  Error: No such option: --no-allow-ordered  Did you mean --allow-ordered?

FIXED while implementing so-u3i, since that issue added a second boolean flag and copying the broken shape was not an option. Boolean flags are now emitted only in their positive form and omitted when off. tests/test_reports.py asserts the absent case explicitly, and the completeness test now turns every boolean on so each must be named.

Filed after the fact so the history exists.
close_reason: Fixed as part of so-u3i; boolean flags now emit only their positive form and tests cover both the present and absent cases.

title: Ingest assumes every measured file is Python, so honouring a project's coverage plugins would crash on template files
description:
read_coverage_db in smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py builds a PythonFileReporter for every row in the coverage database's file table:

    reporter = PythonFileReporter(absolute_path, cov)

coverage.py supports file-type plugins (django_coverage_plugin, mako, jinja) which put NON-Python files into that same table and supply their own FileReporter implementation. Asking PythonFileReporter to parse a .html template will fail, and the failure lands in a code path whose stated stance is that every error is fatal -- so profiling would abort outright on any project using one of these plugins.

LATENT TODAY, REACHABLE THE MOMENT so-asl LANDS. runner.py currently replaces the project's coverage configuration with a minimal rcfile containing only 'branch = True', which discards any configured plugins along with everything else. So the file table is Python-only by accident. so-asl exists precisely to stop discarding the project's config; the moment it does, plugin-registered files start appearing and this crashes. The two must land together.

The correct fix is to ask coverage for the right reporter rather than hard-coding one -- coverage's own reporting layer resolves a FileReporter per file via its plugin registry. Whether non-Python files should then contribute branches to the map at all is a design question worth deciding explicitly rather than falling out of the implementation: a template's 'branches' may not be a meaningful selection signal.
acceptance_criteria: A coverage database containing a file registered by a coverage file-type plugin is ingested without error, and the decision about whether such files contribute branches is documented rather than incidental.

title: Profile JSON is written in non-deterministic order, so two identical profiling runs produce byte-different files
description:
_save_profiling_data in smoke_optimiser/cli.py serialises every frozenset with bare list(), which takes Python's set iteration order:

    branches_covered=list(po.branches_covered)
    files_covered=list(po.files_covered)
    markers=list(po.markers)
    total_branches=list(profiling_data.total_branches)
    measured_files=list(profiling_data.measured_files)
    unattributable_branches=list(profiling_data.unattributable_branches)

Set ordering varies with insertion history and string hashing, so profiling the same tree twice yields JSON that differs everywhere despite describing identical data. That makes profiles impossible to diff, impossible to check into a repository usefully, and hides real changes in the noise -- which matters as soon as anyone wants to see what a code change did to the coverage map.

Sorting is the obvious fix. Note it is six lines, all in one function, which is why this is filed rather than fixed inline. Consider whether sorting belongs in the model layer instead, so anything else that serialises a profile inherits it.

Sizes are modest -- this repository has a few hundred branches, enphase_curtailer's 2600-test suite would be in the low tens of thousands -- so the sort cost is not a concern at realistic scale.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling the same tree twice with no source changes produces byte-identical JSON, ignoring the meta block's timestamp and command.

title: Parallel pytest workers (xdist) would race on the single shared outcomes JSON file
design:
DECIDED 2026-09-06 (user): SUPPORT xdist, do not reject it.

RATIONALE. Half this tool is the coverage map, half is the time-based suite
construction. Wanting only the map is a completely normal use (so-jr5's
change-based selection consumes the map and never reads a duration). Parallel
profiling is fine for that half, so it must not warn loudly at profile time.
Contended durations only matter to the half that uses time, so that is the
half that objects.

CAPTURE. Per-worker outcomes files keyed by PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER, merged by the
runner after the run (union across files). Detection must be RUNTIME, not
arg-string sniffing: xdist can be switched on by the target project's own
pytest.ini addopts, never appearing in --pytest-args, which is the exact
silent-data-loss case this issue is about. The plugin reads PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER
and PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER_COUNT from its own process.

RECORD. The worker count lands in the profile (ProfilingMeta), so the fact
travels with the artefact rather than living in stderr.

CONSUME. The time-based optimiser ERRORS on a profile recorded with >1 worker,
with an explicit override flag to proceed. A coverage-per-second ranking built
on contended timings is confidently wrong and looks fine, so a warning is not
enough. The map-only consumers stay silent.
close_reason: xdist supported: per-worker outcomes files merged by the runner, worker count recorded in the profile, time-based optimiser errors on a parallel profile with an --allow-parallel-durations override. Verified end to end with real pytest-xdist: 93/93 tests captured across 2 workers.

title: check_prerequisites looks for pytest on PATH but the runner invokes it as a module
description:
check_prerequisites gates on pytest being an executable on PATH:

    if shutil.which('pytest') is None:
        raise RuntimeError('pytest not found in PATH')

but every actual invocation runs it as a module of the current interpreter:

    pytest_cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', ...]

The two can disagree in both directions.

FALSE NEGATIVE (the common one): pytest is importable by sys.executable but not
on PATH. This is normal when smoke-optimiser is invoked via 'uv run', via
'python -m', from a virtualenv whose bin directory is not on PATH, or from a
tox/nox session. Profiling is refused even though it would work.

FALSE POSITIVE: a pytest on PATH belonging to a DIFFERENT environment satisfies
the check while sys.executable has no pytest, so the check passes and the
subprocess then fails with 'No module named pytest'.

FIX: test what is actually used -- importlib.util.find_spec('pytest') against
the running interpreter -- and say which interpreter was checked when it fails.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py:58

NOTE: tests/test_runner.py::test_check_prerequisites_success patches
shutil.which, so the patch target moves with the fix.

ACCEPTANCE: profiling proceeds in an environment where pytest is importable but
absent from PATH.

title: Line-level change-based selection, with git-aware remapping of shifted line numbers
description:
so-jr5 deliberately ships FILE-level change-based selection: a changed file
selects every test that has ever executed any line in it. This is the follow-up
that narrows it to the lines actually touched.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE FIRST. Line numbers shift. Insert one line at the top of a
file and every line number below it moves, so a line-level map silently
mismatches after almost any edit -- and silent mismatch means silent
under-selection, the one failure mode this feature must never have. File-level
is immune to line shifts, reformatting, and refactors within a file.

WHAT THIS NEEDS. Git-aware remapping: track how lines moved between the commit
the profile was taken at (ProfilingMeta.commit is already recorded) and HEAD, so
a profiled line number still resolves to the right line today. `git diff -U0`
between those two commits gives the hunks to translate through.

DO NOT START THIS UNTIL file-level has been measured in real use. On enphase the
file-level map has a median of 37 tests per file out of 2600 -- if that is
already fast enough, the extra precision buys nothing and costs a whole
remapping layer that can be subtly wrong.
